chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:
I asked him about a man who looks into the private part of his wife while he is having intercourse with her. He said, 'There is no harm in it, except that it causes blindness in the child.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it/permissible

ai.seo_question: Does a husband looking at his wife's private parts during intercourse have any negative effects on their children?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Samaanah reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits a husband to gaze at his wife’s private parts during intercourse, noting it is not inherently sinful but carries a specific physical consequence: it may cause blindness in their offspring. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between permissibility (ibahah) and recommended caution (istihbab) based on potential bodily effects, reflecting the tradition's attention to both legal status and physiological wisdom.
